r_det: ASSUMPTION predator detection range (set equal to r_burst so detection races the strike; 6 m is a sensitivity case)
t_refract: ASSUMPTION time before a landed fish can re-launch
glide_cv: ASSUMPTION per-launch lognormal CV of airborne distance/time
U_flee: ASSUMPTION non-glider flee speed (~10 SL/s for a 17 cm fish)
r0: ASSUMPTION predator start distance from school centroid
r_burst: ASSUMPTION distance at which the predator bursts
kappa: ASSUMPTION confusion strength in water (Landeau & Terborgh form)
kappa_air: ASSUMPTION confusion from simultaneous airborne fish
r_view: ASSUMPTION predator view radius for retargeting / aerial confusion

a_LW: FishBase Hyporhamphus LW used for the whole walk (body shape is not an evolving trait here)
w_body_frac: body width / SL for span; assumption
V_exit: water-exit speed, same for all phenotypes; Fish 1990 citing Shoulejkin gives ~10 m/s before taxiing (secondary)
dV_taxi: max taxi speed gain at full asymmetry and full aerodynamic support; 10 -> 18 m/s midpoint of Fish 1990/Shoulejkin 16-20
e_swim: escape probability of a prey that does not leave the water, per attack; assumption
U_burst: predator burst speed; inside FishBase Thunnus albacares burst rows 5.21-20.46 m/s
U_sus: predator sustained speed; FishBase Coryphaena hippurus sustained row
d_gap: H_chase: distance scale over which a lead beyond the predator's chase breaks pursuit; assumption
d_vis: H_vis: distance scale over which an airborne excursion breaks visual tracking (inf = off); assumption
beta_air: aerial predator hazard while airborne; assumption
p_max: Davenport 1992 limit on pectoral length / SL
n_trim: CL rule: commanded lift at exit <= n_trim x weight (1.0 = level at exit); 1.5 lets fast fish climb (argon review)
kappa_fin: aquatic cost of fins: survival/fecundity factor exp(-kappa_fin * fin wetted area / body wetted area); 0 = escape-only fitness; added after argon review
k_wet: body wetted area = k_wet SL^2 (ASSUMPTION for a slender fusiform fish)
